title: The Cat Who Walked on the Copy
synopsis: The plaster copy has a paw print on its back.
Rome's ruins are home to many cats.
One of them may know who made the copy.
goal: Find the workshop that made the plaster copy, and who ordered it.

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene) of the cat ruins: the cat board is read, then the cats on the stones are looked at. Two cats are orange: the board's 'short tail' and 'plaster workshop' (the copy is plaster) pick Tito, never the colour alone.
No recall here: the evidence card is not tried over a look round; the copy is named by a text mention.

play.title: The Cat Board
story: Old Roman temples stand in a square below the street.
Cats sleep on the warm stones.
In the copy's paw print, Giulia finds one short orange hair.
play.letter:
CATS WHO VISIT US
ROSSO — orange, with a long, fluffy tail. He lives at the fish shop.
TITO — orange, with a short tail. He lives at a plaster workshop.
LUNA — black, with a long tail. She lives at the bakery.
play.question: Which cat walked on the wet plaster copy?
hints: Find the board about the cats and read it first.
The hair is orange, and the copy is plaster. Which cat lives with plaster?
transition: Orange hair and a plaster workshop. It must be Tito!
"Tito comes here every day at noon," says a woman with cat food.
And there he is, jumping down from a column.

discovery.title: TITO THE CAT
discovery.detail: Orange, with a short tail, and he lives with plaster. Follow Tito!

notes: Letter: Tito's round collar tag, S I B A S in a circle. From the big B, round to the right: B A S S I.

clueInputs.note: Tito lives at a plaster workshop.

play.title: Tito's Round Tag
story: Tito rubs his head on your shoes.
He has a round metal tag on his collar.
The letters go all the way round the circle.
play.letter:
The letters go round in a circle:
S · I · B · A · S
(The B is big. After the last S, the circle goes back to the first S.)

A note on the back: Start at the big letter. Go round to the right.
play.question: Read Tito's tag from the big letter. Spell his family's name.
hints: Start with B. The next letters are A, then S.
At the end, the circle goes back to the start.
transition: B, A, S, S, I. Tito belongs to the Bassi family.
"The Bassi workshop is around the corner," says the cat woman.
Tito walks in front of you, tail up, as if he knows the way.
play.orderFeedback: Every letter is on the tag. Start at the big B and go round.

play.title: How a Copy Is Made
story: The workshop is full of white statues and white dust.
Tito jumps onto the work table.
On the wall is a sign for visitors.
play.letter:
HOW WE MAKE A COPY
Then, we pour wet plaster into the mould.
First, we press soft rubber around the real thing. This makes a mould.
Last, we paint the copy to look like old stone.
After the plaster is dry, we take the copy out.
play.question: Put the steps in order. How is a copy made?
hints: Find First. What do you need before you can pour plaster?
play.successMessage: You know how a copy is made!
transition: Carla opens her big order book.
"I keep every order," she says. "Let's look."
play.orderFeedback: Read First, Then, After and Last again.

clue.title: How a Copy Is Made

play.title: Order Number 3?8
story: "Every order card is in a locked drawer," she says.
"Each drawer opens with its order number."
play.letter:
ORDERS — THIS WEEK
317 — A stone shell, for a garden. Done on Monday.
318 — An old map piece, for "a museum friend". Paid in cash. Done on Thursday.
319 — A lion's head, for a hotel. Not done yet.
play.question: Which order is the map copy? Turn the dials to its number.
hints: Look at the back of the plaster copy in your Notebook: No. 3?8.

transition: The man with the copy had the real piece on Tuesday.
On Thursday, he took the copy away.
And on Tuesday, a grumpy professor was here, too.

objectives: Find the cat that walked on the copy.
intro: The plaster copy has a tiny paw print on its back.
"Rome has lots of cats," says Giulia. "And they love the old ruins."
"Let's ask the cats of Torre Argentina!"
play.caseSummary: An orange hair led to Tito the cat and his home, the Bassi workshop. A copy is made from a mould of the real thing. So someone brought the real piece there on Tuesday. On Thursday, a big man in a yellow helmet picked up order 318.

notes: Act 2 opens: who made the copy, and who had the real piece. Order card 318 (s3_ep05_e4) is used again in Case 10 and Case 11.
Carla Bassi made the copy in good faith: she was told the museum sent him.
STEP 3-14: M1 is now a look round the cat ruins ending in a choice of three cats (new pictures); two are orange, so the board's words decide. Carla's talks, Discovery Moments and an ending added.
